units.laminate: A N/m, B N, D N*m

caliper_mm.basis: sum over the layers; 4 layers × 0.2 mm, rectilinear rasters [0, 90, 90, 0] (cycled), infill 1; lamina: bead direction E = infill × E_xy, cross-bead E = infill × E_z (the inter-layer bond standing in for the inter-bead bond), G = √(E_L·E_T)/(2(1+ν)), linear in infill (an upper bound for sparse fill); Bambu Lab, TPU 95A HF Technical Data Sheet V1.0: Young's modulus X-Y 9.8 ± 0.7 MPa and Z 7.4 ± 0.6 MPa (ISO 527), density 1.22 g/cm³ (ISO 1183) — https://store.bblcdn.com/58df32731eab4c90a7dac9b12e13ba88.pdf; that sheet is the HF grade, the card names TPU 95A; assumed ν = 0.45: a 95A elastomer is nearly incompressible (ν → 0.5) and printed voids lower it; no datasheet states it

notes: perimeters and walls are ignored: the print is treated as its raster infill
crease: an elastomer print recovers rather than creases; no crease block
crease and contact are not computed for a stack: a laminate's crease is not its layers' creases
